req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with the same body for the same task_id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates PUT idempotency: repeating the same PUT request with the same body and task_id must yield the same terminal state. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — two identical PUTs produce identical 200 responses with matching fields; (2) negative NEG — PUT on a non-existent task_id returns 404 both times, confirming idempotent error behavior; (3) boundary BVA — PUT with max-length title (100 chars) and max-length description (500 chars) repeated twice yields identical 200 responses; (4) STC — PUT transitions a task from incomplete to complete, then repeating the same PUT leaves state unchanged; (5) DT — PUT with only the 'completed' field (partial update) repeated twice yields identical state, catching mutations in partial-update logic.

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_positive_same_response_twice
preconditions: Task with id=7 exists: title='Fix login bug', completed=false
Database is pre-loaded with seed data
actions: POST in-process FastAPI TestClient with PUT /tasks/7 body {title='Fixed login bug', description='Ember willow nova meridian flux cascade zenith.', completed=true}
Record response1 status and JSON
Repeat identical PUT /tasks/7 with same body
Record response2 status and JSON
expected: Both responses return HTTP 200
response1.json() fields id, title, description, completed match response2.json() fields exactly
title == 'Fixed login bug', completed == true, id == 7
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app
import sqlalchemy, os
from app.database import Base

os.environ.setdefault('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite:///./test_idem_pos.db')
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app import models
from app.database import get_db

engine = create_engine('sqlite:///./test_idem_pos.db', connect_args={'check_same_thread': False})
Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine)
Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)
Session = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
db = Session()
db.add(models.Task(id=7, title='Fix login bug', description='Ember willow nova meridian flux cascade zenith.', completed=False))
db.commit()
db.close()

def override_get_db():
    db = Session()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

body = {'title': 'Fixed login bug', 'description': 'Ember willow nova meridian flux cascade zenith.', 'completed': True}
r1 = client.put('/tasks/7', json=body)
r2 = client.put('/tasks/7', json=body)
assert r1.status_code == 200
assert r2.status_code == 200
j1 = r1.json()
j2 = r2.json()
assert j1['id'] == 7
assert j2['id'] == 7
assert j1['title'] == 'Fixed login bug'
assert j2['title'] == 'Fixed login bug'
assert j1['completed'] == True
assert j2['completed'] == True
assert j1['description'] == 'Ember willow nova meridian flux cascade zenith.'
assert j2['description'] == 'Ember willow nova meridian flux cascade zenith.'
assert j1['title'] == j2['title']
assert j1['completed'] == j2['completed']
assert j1['description'] == j2['description']
assert j1['id'] == j2['id']
app.dependency_overrides.clear()

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_state_transition_incomplete_to_complete
preconditions: Task with id=4 exists: title='Prepare meeting agenda', completed=false
Database is pre-loaded with seed data
actions: GET /tasks/4 to confirm initial state completed=false
PUT /tasks/4 with {title='Prepare meeting agenda', completed=true}
GET /tasks/4 to confirm state is now completed=true
PUT /tasks/4 again with identical body {title='Prepare meeting agenda', completed=true}
GET /tasks/4 to confirm state is still completed=true (no regression)
expected: Initial GET returns completed=false
First PUT returns HTTP 200 with completed=true
Second PUT returns HTTP 200 with completed=true
Final GET returns completed=true — state is stable after repeated PUT

from app.main import app
